<result># Feed vs. Folders Navigation — Current State of Unification

## 1. `model/types.ts` — shared node shape

**File:** `/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/model/types.ts`

```ts
// Shared node shapes for the notes navigation surface.
// Folder trees and feed buckets both fit this contract.
export type NavigationNode = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  children: NavigationNode[];
  noteCount?: number;
  notes?: NoteEntry[];
};
```

This is the one type both views are rendered through — `TreeNode`/`TreeRow` take `node: NavigationNode`. But it is a **structural, not nominal**, unification:

- Real folder data flows in as `TreeItem` (same file, lines 13-20), which extends the shape with `collapsed?: boolean`, produced by `notes-tree-model.ts` / `tree-ops.ts` from the real `FolderNode` tree.
- Feed data flows in as `FeedTreeNode` (`/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/model/feed-tree-model.ts` lines 15-27), which has many feed-only fields (`kind`, `parentId`, `rangeStartMs`, `rangeEndMs`, `latestMs`, `rank`) plus `id/name/children/notes/noteCount` that happen to satisfy `NavigationNode` structurally.

So `FeedTreeNode` and `TreeItem` are **completely separate declared types** — there is no explicit union or shared interface they both `extends`. They only interoperate because `FeedTreeNode` happens to be a structural superset of `NavigationNode`, which is what gets passed down into `TreeNode`. There's no adapter/normalizer function that converts folder-or-feed data into one canonical node before rendering; the raw model objects are passed straight through.

## 2. `use-tree-interactions.ts` — how generic is it?

**File:** `/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/app/hooks/use-tree-interactions.ts`

This hook is **folder-specific**, not generic over both trees:
- `handleFolderClick` (line 120) computes range selection over `orderedIds` from `useNotesTree()` (the real folder tree's flattened id order), and calls `findNode(tree, ...)` (folder-only tree op) inside `handleNoteClick` (line 176-178) to resolve a note's siblings.
- It reads `tree, orderedIds, setExpanded, shouldNestNotesInNavigation` from `useNotesTree()` — none of that is feed-aware.
- `handleToggle` (line 135) is generic (just toggles an id in the `expanded` Set), so that part could work for either tree, but it's exported/used only from the folders side.

Feed does **its own thing** entirely: `FeedPanel` (`ui/feed-panel.tsx`) reimplements the equivalent handlers locally — `selectFeedGroup` (line 64), `handleNoteSelect` (line 93), `handleToggle` (line 128, functionally identical to the one in `use-tree-interactions.ts`), and `handleNoteContextMenu` (line 144). export function computeRangeSelection(
  event: SelectionModifiers,
  current: Set<string>,
  order: string[],
  lastSelected: string | null,
  path: string
): Set<string> {
  const next = new Set(current);
  if (event.shiftKey && lastSelected) {
    next.clear();
    const start = order.indexOf(lastSelected);
    const end = order.indexOf(path);
    if (start !== -1 && end !== -1) {
      const [from, to] = start < end ? [start, end] : [end, start];
      order.slice(from, to + 1).forEach((id) => next.add(id));
    } else {
      next.add(path);
    }
  } else if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) {
    if (next.has(path)) next.delete(path);
    else next.add(path);
  } else {
    next.clear();
    next.add(path);
  }
  return next;
}
```

export function computeRangeSelection(
  event: SelectionModifiers,
  current: Set<string>,
  order: string[],
  lastSelected: string | null,
  path: string
): Set<string> {
  const next = new Set(current);
  if (event.shiftKey && lastSelected) {
    next.clear();
    const start = order.indexOf(lastSelected);
    const end = order.indexOf(path);
    if (start !== -1 && end !== -1) {
      const [from, to] = start < end ? [start, end] : [end, start];
      order.slice(from, to + 1).forEach((id) => next.add(id));
    } else {
      next.add(path);
    }
  } else if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) {
    if (next.has(path)) next.delete(path);
    else next.add(path);
  } else {
    next.clear();
    next.add(path);
  }
  return next;
}
```

## 3. Tree model (`notes-tree-model.ts`) and traversal (`tree-ops.ts`)

`TreeItem` (types.ts:13-20):
```ts
export type TreeItem = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  children: TreeItem[];
  noteCount?: number;
  notes?: NoteEntry[];
  collapsed?: boolean;
};
```
`NavigationNode` (types.ts:5-11) is the same shape minus `collapsed`, used by both Feed buckets and Folders as a common contract.

`buildTreeItems` (`tree-ops.ts:8-16`) turns the backend `FolderNode` (real filesystem folder tree) into `TreeItem[]` recursively — this is what makes "Folders" the *real* user tree vs. Feed's synthetic date buckets (built by `feed-tree-model.ts`, not covered here since you didn't ask about it in depth).

Traversal/mutation helpers you'll want for reference:
- `flattenTreeData`/`flattenTree` (tree-ops.ts:25-38, dnd-tree.ts:35-52) — depth-first flatten with `depth`/`parentId`, used to build `orderedIds` (flat top-to-bottom order) for shift-click ranges and arrow-key nav.

### 4c. Shift-click multi-select (shared by both trees)

`/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/shared/lib/selection.ts:18-44` — `computeRangeSelection(event, current, order, lastSelected, path)`:
```ts
if (event.shiftKey && lastSelected) {
  next.clear();
  const start = order.indexOf(lastSelected);
  const end = order.indexOf(path);
  if (start !== -1 && end !== -1) {
    const [from, to] = start < end ? [start, end] : [end, start];
    order.slice(from, to + 1).forEach((id) => next.add(id));
  } else { next.add(path); }
} else if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) {
  next.has(path) ? next.delete(path) : next.add(path);
} else { next.clear(); next.add(path); }
```
Called from `handleFolderClick` (`use-tree-interactions.ts:120-133`) with `orderedIds` (flat DFS order from `flattenTreeData`) as `order`. Both Feed and Folders reuse this exact function — the range is purely index-based over the flattened id list, agnostic of which row component renders it, so shift-click behavior itself is identical between the two views; only the visual selected style differs (see 4a/4b above).

## 5. Fonts

- App-wide base: `:root { font-family: "Avenir Next", "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.35; }` (`app.css:8-11`). **`font-size:14px` on `:root` is important**: Tailwind's rem-based text utilities (`text-sm = 0.875rem`, `text-xs = 0.75rem`, etc.) resolve relative to this root, i.e. `text-sm` actually computes to `0.875 × 14px ≈ 12.25px`, not the "expected" 14px you'd get on a standard 16px-root page.
- Feed / dead-code Folders stack (`app.css:717-722, 643-646`):
  ```css
  .tree-pane .item-label { color: var(--ui-text); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0; }
  .tree-pane .nav-note-row .item-label { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 450; }
  ```
  These are hard-coded pixel values, unaffected by root font-size shrinkage.
- Folders (actual, Tailwind stack): folder label is a bare `<span>{node.name}</span>` inside `SidebarMenuButton`, which only supplies `text-sm` (≈12.25px per above) and no explicit `font-weight` (browser default 400) unless `data-active=true`, which adds `font-medium` (500). Note label is a bare `<span>` inside `SidebarMenuSubButton` with `size="md"` → `text-sm` also, again default weight 400 unless active.

So in practice: Folders' un-selected text renders **smaller** (~12.25px, weight 400) than Feed's (14px folders / 13px notes, weight 500/450) — the opposite of "bigger/bolder." Whichever one visually "looks better" to you, this is the exact mechanical cause: Feed uses fixed-px custom CSS; Folders uses Tailwind rem utilities riding on top of a shrunk 14px root font-size, so its effective computed sizes are smaller than they'd be on an unmodified Tailwind setup.

## 6. Indentation — folders vs. inline notes in nested mode

This is the one that matters most for your "crooked" complaint, and the two stacks compute it completely differently.

### 6a. Dead-code / Feed stack (`TreeRow` / `NavNoteRow`) — numeric padding formula

`TreeRow` (`tree-row.tsx:78-84`):
```ts
const style = {
  transform: isDragging ? undefined : CSS.Translate.toString(transform),
  paddingLeft: 12 + depth * indentationWidth,
} as React.CSSProperties;
const guideBaseLeft = feedMode
  ? 12 + indentationWidth / 2         // feed folders: 12 + 9  = 21
  : 12 + 20 + 6 + 8;                  // real folders: 12+20+6+8 = 46 (unreachable in prod)
```
`NavNoteRow` (`nav-note-row.tsx:55-59`):
```ts
const style = {
  transform: isDragging ? undefined : CSS.Translate.toString(transform),
  paddingLeft: 12 + depth * indentationWidth,
};
const guideBaseLeft = 12 + indentationWidth / 2;   // always 21, regardless of feedMode
```
`indentationWidth` is the shared constant `18` (`/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/shared/constants.ts:3`, also hardcoded as `18` in `feed-panel.tsx:234`). Notes are rendered by `TreeNode` at `depth: depth + 1` relative to their parent folder (`tree-node.tsx:99-106`), same formula as a sibling subfolder, so the raw `paddingLeft` numbers line up between a folder and its inline notes.

**But** `NavNoteRow` only draws its `tree-guides` (the vertical connector lines) `showGuides && depth > 0` (`nav-note-row.tsx:75`), and `showGuides={feedMode}` is passed from `TreeNode` (`tree-node.tsx:111`). So:
- In Feed (`feedMode=true`): folder guides use `guideBaseLeft = 21` and note guides use `guideBaseLeft = 21` — **same formula, consistent.**
- In the dead-code Folders branch (`feedMode=false`): folder guides use the hardcoded `46` (a magic number derived from `12(padding) + 20(toggle width) + 6(gap) + 8(half of glyph width)`, not expressed in terms of `indentationWidth`), while notes get `showGuides=false` → **no guide lines drawn for notes at all**, even though the padding-left number would put them at the same x-offset. If this branch were ever used, notes would sit at the "correct" numeric indent but with no connecting line, next to sibling folders that do have one — a real inconsistency, though moot since this branch never renders in production.

### 6b. Actual production stack (`SidebarFileTreeNode`) — the real bug

Indentation here is **not** a per-row numeric `depth * width` formula at all; it's nested `<ul>` margin/padding via `SidebarMenuSub` (sidebar.tsx:638-651):
```
"border-sidebar-border mx-3.5 flex min-w-0 translate-x-px flex-col gap-1 border-l px-2.5 py-0.5"
```
`mx-3.5` = 14px left margin (this is also where the `border-l` guide-line sits), `px-2.5` = 10px left padding → each nesting level shifts child content right by margin(14) + padding(10) = **24px total**, and the vertical guide line renders at the 14px mark.

Both notes (`SidebarMenuSubButton`) and subfolders (recursed `SidebarFileTreeNode` → `SidebarMenuButton`) are children of the *same* `<SidebarMenuSub>`, so they get identical outer indent. The crookedness comes from what's rendered **inside** the row, before the label:

- Folder row (`sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx:89-105`) always reserves a leading icon slot of fixed width before the `<Folder />` glyph:
  ```tsx
  {hasNestedItems ? (
    <button className="sidebar-filetree-toggle"> {/* 14x14, sidebar.tsx via app.css:325-337 */}
      <ChevronRight className="sidebar-filetree-chevron ..." />
    </button>
  ) : (
    <span className="sidebar-filetree-toggle-spacer" aria-hidden /> {/* 14x14 placeholder, app.css:353-358 */}
  )}
  <Folder />
  ```
  i.e. **every** folder row, expandable or not, has a 14px chevron/spacer + `gap:8px` (from `.sidebar-filetree-button-inner { gap: 8px }`, app.css:317-323) = 22px reserved before its folder icon.

- Note row (`sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx:135-159`) has **no equivalent leading spacer at all**:
  ```tsx
  <button type="button" className="sidebar-filetree-note-button">
    <File />
    <span>{preview?.title || note.name}</span>
    ...
  </button>
  ```
  It jumps straight to the `<File />` icon.

**Net effect:** at the same nesting depth, a folder's label starts ~22px further right than a sibling note's label (chevron/spacer width 14px + gap 8px that folders reserve and notes don't), even though both rows sit inside the exact same `<SidebarMenuSub>` with identical margin/padding. This is the concrete, file-and-line-verifiable source of the "crooked" nested-notes indentation you're seeing when `shouldNestNotesInNavigation` (`notesListMode === "nested"`, set in `use-notes-tree-state.ts:83`) is on — notes visually float ~22px to the left of their sibling subfolders' labels because the note button never renders the leading toggle/spacer element that folder buttons always do.

(For contrast, the never-rendered `NavNoteRow`/`TreeRow` pair got this right: `NavNoteRow` always renders a matching `<span className="icon-spacer" />` — same `.tree-pane .icon-spacer { width: 20px; height: 22px; }` as `.tree-pane .tree-toggle { width: 20px; height: 22px; }` — so folder and note icons/labels align perfectly there. `SidebarFileTreeNode` is missing that equivalent spacer for its note button.)

## 3. Tree model (`notes-tree-model.ts`) and traversal (`tree-ops.ts`)

```ts
export type TreeItem = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  children: TreeItem[];
  noteCount?: number;
  notes?: NoteEntry[];
  collapsed?: boolean;
};
```
`NavigationNode` (types.ts:5-11) is the same shape minus `collapsed`, used by both Feed buckets and Folders as a common contract.

`buildTreeItems` (`tree-ops.ts:8-16`) turns the backend `FolderNode` (real filesystem folder tree) into `TreeItem[]` recursively — this is what makes "Folders" the *real* user tree vs. Feed's synthetic date buckets (built by `feed-tree-model.ts`, not covered here since you didn't ask about it in depth).

Traversal/mutation helpers you'll want for reference:
- `flattenTreeData`/`flattenTree` (tree-ops.ts:25-38, dnd-tree.ts:35-52) — depth-first flatten with `depth`/`parentId`, used to build `orderedIds` (flat top-to-bottom order) for shift-click ranges and arrow-key nav.

- `parseDropTargetId`/`DropTarget` (tree-ops.ts:193-218) — decodes `drop:<id>:<inside|before|after>` ids produced by `dropId()` (tree-dnd.ts:7).

### 4c. Shift-click multi-select (shared by both trees)

`/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/shared/lib/selection.ts:18-44` — `computeRangeSelection(event, current, order, lastSelected, path)`:
```ts
if (event.shiftKey && lastSelected) {
  next.clear();
  const start = order.indexOf(lastSelected);
  const end = order.indexOf(path);
  if (start !== -1 && end !== -1) {
    const [from, to] = start < end ? [start, end] : [end, start];
    order.slice(from, to + 1).forEach((id) => next.add(id));
  } else { next.add(path); }
} else if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) {
  next.has(path) ? next.delete(path) : next.add(path);
} else { next.clear(); next.add(path); }
```
Called from `handleFolderClick` (`use-tree-interactions.ts:120-133`) with `orderedIds` (flat DFS order from `flattenTreeData`) as `order`. Both Feed and Folders reuse this exact function — the range is purely index-based over the flattened id list, agnostic of which row component renders it, so shift-click behavior itself is identical between the two views; only the visual selected style differs (see 4a/4b above).

## 5. Fonts

- App-wide base: `:root { font-family: "Avenir Next", "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.35; }` (`app.css:8-11`). **`font-size:14px` on `:root` is important**: Tailwind's rem-based text utilities (`text-sm = 0.875rem`, `text-xs = 0.75rem`, etc.) resolve relative to this root, i.e. `text-sm` actually computes to `0.875 × 14px ≈ 12.25px`, not the "expected" 14px you'd get on a standard 16px-root page.
- Feed / dead-code Folders stack (`app.css:717-722, 643-646`):
  ```css
  .tree-pane .item-label { color: var(--ui-text); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0; }
  .tree-pane .nav-note-row .item-label { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 450; }
  ```
  These are hard-coded pixel values, unaffected by root font-size shrinkage.
- Folders (actual, Tailwind stack): folder label is a bare `<span>{node.name}</span>` inside `SidebarMenuButton`, which only supplies `text-sm` (≈12.25px per above) and no explicit `font-weight` (browser default 400) unless `data-active=true`, which adds `font-medium` (500). Note label is a bare `<span>` inside `SidebarMenuSubButton` with `size="md"` → `text-sm` also, again default weight 400 unless active.

So in practice: Folders' un-selected text renders **smaller** (~12.25px, weight 400) than Feed's (14px folders / 13px notes, weight 500/450) — the opposite of "bigger/bolder." Whichever one visually "looks better" to you, this is the exact mechanical cause: Feed uses fixed-px custom CSS; Folders uses Tailwind rem utilities riding on top of a shrunk 14px root font-size, so its effective computed sizes are smaller than they'd be on an unmodified Tailwind setup.

## 6. Indentation — folders vs. inline notes in nested mode

This is the one that matters most for your "crooked" complaint, and the two stacks compute it completely differently.

### 6a. Dead-code / Feed stack (`TreeRow` / `NavNoteRow`) — numeric padding formula

`TreeRow` (`tree-row.tsx:78-84`):
```ts
const style = {
  transform: isDragging ? undefined : CSS.Translate.toString(transform),
  paddingLeft: 12 + depth * indentationWidth,
} as React.CSSProperties;
const guideBaseLeft = feedMode
  ? 12 + indentationWidth / 2         // feed folders: 12 + 9  = 21
  : 12 + 20 + 6 + 8;                  // real folders: 12+20+6+8 = 46 (unreachable in prod)
```
`NavNoteRow` (`nav-note-row.tsx:55-59`):
```ts
const style = {
  transform: isDragging ? undefined : CSS.Translate.toString(transform),
  paddingLeft: 12 + depth * indentationWidth,
};
const guideBaseLeft = 12 + indentationWidth / 2;   // always 21, regardless of feedMode
```
`indentationWidth` is the shared constant `18` (`/home/sprite/type/apps/desktop/src/shared/constants.ts:3`, also hardcoded as `18` in `feed-panel.tsx:234`). Notes are rendered by `TreeNode` at `depth: depth + 1` relative to their parent folder (`tree-node.tsx:99-106`), same formula as a sibling subfolder, so the raw `paddingLeft` numbers line up between a folder and its inline notes.

**But** `NavNoteRow` only draws its `tree-guides` (the vertical connector lines) `showGuides && depth > 0` (`nav-note-row.tsx:75`), and `showGuides={feedMode}` is passed from `TreeNode` (`tree-node.tsx:111`). So:
- In Feed (`feedMode=true`): folder guides use `guideBaseLeft = 21` and note guides use `guideBaseLeft = 21` — **same formula, consistent.**
- In the dead-code Folders branch (`feedMode=false`): folder guides use the hardcoded `46` (a magic number derived from `12(padding) + 20(toggle width) + 6(gap) + 8(half of glyph width)`, not expressed in terms of `indentationWidth`), while notes get `showGuides=false` → **no guide lines drawn for notes at all**, even though the padding-left number would put them at the same x-offset. If this branch were ever used, notes would sit at the "correct" numeric indent but with no connecting line, next to sibling folders that do have one — a real inconsistency, though moot since this branch never renders in production.

### 6b. Actual production stack (`SidebarFileTreeNode`) — the real bug

Indentation here is **not** a per-row numeric `depth * width` formula at all; it's nested `<ul>` margin/padding via `SidebarMenuSub` (sidebar.tsx:638-651):
```
"border-sidebar-border mx-3.5 flex min-w-0 translate-x-px flex-col gap-1 border-l px-2.5 py-0.5"
```
`mx-3.5` = 14px left margin (this is also where the `border-l` guide-line sits), `px-2.5` = 10px left padding → each nesting level shifts child content right by margin(14) + padding(10) = **24px total**, and the vertical guide line renders at the 14px mark.

Both notes (`SidebarMenuSubButton`) and subfolders (recursed `SidebarFileTreeNode` → `SidebarMenuButton`) are children of the *same* `<SidebarMenuSub>`, so they get identical outer indent. The crookedness comes from what's rendered **inside** the row, before the label:

- Folder row (`sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx:89-105`) always reserves a leading icon slot of fixed width before the `<Folder />` glyph:
  ```tsx
  {hasNestedItems ? (
    <button className="sidebar-filetree-toggle"> {/* 14x14, sidebar.tsx via app.css:325-337 */}
      <ChevronRight className="sidebar-filetree-chevron ..." />
    </button>
  ) : (
    <span className="sidebar-filetree-toggle-spacer" aria-hidden /> {/* 14x14 placeholder, app.css:353-358 */}
  )}
  <Folder />
  ```
  i.e. **every** folder row, expandable or not, has a 14px chevron/spacer + `gap:8px` (from `.sidebar-filetree-button-inner { gap: 8px }`, app.css:317-323) = 22px reserved before its folder icon.

- Note row (`sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx:135-159`) has **no equivalent leading spacer at all**:
  ```tsx
  <button type="button" className="sidebar-filetree-note-button">
    <File />
    <span>{preview?.title || note.name}</span>
    ...
  </button>
  ```
  It jumps straight to the `<File />` icon.

**Net effect:** at the same nesting depth, a folder's label starts ~22px further right than a sibling note's label (chevron/spacer width 14px + gap 8px that folders reserve and notes don't), even though both rows sit inside the exact same `<SidebarMenuSub>` with identical margin/padding. This is the concrete, file-and-line-verifiable source of the "crooked" nested-notes indentation you're seeing when `shouldNestNotesInNavigation` (`notesListMode === "nested"`, set in `use-notes-tree-state.ts:83`) is on — notes visually float ~22px to the left of their sibling subfolders' labels because the note button never renders the leading toggle/spacer element that folder buttons always do.

(For contrast, the never-rendered `NavNoteRow`/`TreeRow` pair got this right: `NavNoteRow` always renders a matching `<span className="icon-spacer" />` — same `.tree-pane .icon-spacer { width: 20px; height: 22px; }` as `.tree-pane .tree-toggle { width: 20px; height: 22px; }` — so folder and note icons/labels align perfectly there. `SidebarFileTreeNode` is missing that equivalent spacer for its note button.)

## 7. Drag-and-drop wiring (fully implemented, currently orphaned for Folders)

- `DndContext` set up once in `desktop-app-shell.tsx:410-418`:
  ```tsx
  <DndContext
    sensors={sensors}
    collisionDetection={pointerWithin}
    onDragStart={handleDragStart}
    onDragMove={handleDragMove}
    onDragOver={handleDragOver}
    onDragEnd={handleDragEnd}
    onDragCancel={handleDragCancel}
  >
  ```
  `sensors = useSensors(useSensor(PointerSensor, { activationConstraint: { distance: 6 } }))` (line 300-302). `DragOverlay` renders a `.drag-ghost` div showing the dragged id's basename (lines 463-467).
- All five handlers come from `useDragDrop` (`hooks/use-drag-drop.ts`, 506 lines, read in full):
  - `handleDragStart` (85-117): distinguishes `data.type === "folder"` vs `"note"` from `DragData`; seeds selection if the dragged item wasn't already selected.
  - `handleDragMove` (119-211): computes `EdgeSnap` (`"before"|"after"|null`) by comparing pointer Y against the hovered row's rect, using a threshold of `Math.min(14, height * 0.35)`; also implements "spring-load" auto-expand of a collapsed folder after hovering 500ms (`expandTimeoutRef`).
  - `handleFolderDragEnd` (223-367): resolves the actual drop target (edge-snap overrides the raw `over.id`), guards against dropping onto itself/its own subtree or system folders (`isSystemFolder`), does an optimistic `removeNodes`/`insertNodes` tree rewrite, calls `moveItems()` for folders whose parent changed, diffs and persists per-parent order via `setOrder()`, and only calls `refreshTree()` if a reparent actually happened.
  - `handleNoteDragEnd` (371-466): moves notes to a folder or to another note's parent, or reorders within the same parent via `reorderList()` + `setOrder()`.

content.text:
Собрал полную картину. Ключевая находка: Feed и Folders сегодня — это два физически разных стека компонентов, не просто разный CSS:

- **Feed** → `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` (ручной CSS в `app.css` + dnd-kit, но с `draggable={false}`)
- **Folders** → `SidebarFileTreeNode` (shadcn/Tailwind Sidebar-примитивы, **без** dnd-kit вообще — это осознанное решение из твоего коммита "Simplify notes navigation surfaces")

Это объясняет всё, что ты описал:
- **Hover на всю ширину** — у Feed `.item-row` растянут edge-to-edge с квадратными углами; у Folders shadcn `SidebarMenuButton` даёт `rounded-md` пилюлю, вписанную в отступы `SidebarGroup` — отсюда ощущение "более зажато".
- **Шрифт** — у Folders текст сейчас технически *меньше* (Tailwind `text-sm` считается от `:root{font-size:14px}`, получается ~12.25px, обычный вес, bold только когда активен) против фиксированных 14px/13px у Feed (вес 500/450 всегда). Механически противоположно тому, что можно было ожидать — нужно уточнить, что именно тебе нравится.
- **Кривая индентация вложенных заметок** — подтверждено: `SidebarFileTreeNode` для строки папки всегда резервирует место под шеврон+гэп (~22px) перед иконкой, а для строки заметки — нет вообще такого отступа. У `NavNoteRow` (уже в Feed-стеке) это уже правильно сделано через одинаковый `icon-spacer`/`tree-toggle` (20px). Просто переход на общий стек чинит это автоматически.
- Бонус: `SidebarFileTreeNode` вообще не умеет drag-and-drop (нет `useDraggable`/`useDroppable`) — то есть сейчас в Folders **нет** ручного перетаскивания/реордера, хотя вся инфраструктура (`useDragDrop`, `tree-ops.ts`) на это рассчитана и уже работает в TreeRow.

Раз ты просил именно единую **визуальную и компонентную** базу — логичный путь: перевести `FoldersPanel` на тот же стек `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`, что уже использует Feed (а не наоборот), и вывести `SidebarFileTreeNode` из употребления. Тогда расхождения превращаются в настройку общих CSS-параметров, а не поддержку двух деревьев. Прежде чем писать план, уточню несколько развилок.

input.description: Design plan for unifying Feed/Folders tree UI
input.prompt:
Repo: /home/sprite/type (Tauri desktop app, apps/desktop/src/). This is a React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind desktop notes app. I need a detailed, file-level implementation plan for a UI/component-unification task described below. Do NOT write code, just produce a step-by-step implementation plan referencing exact files/functions.

## Background (confirmed via prior codebase exploration)

The desktop app's left-side note navigation has two tabs: "Feed" (pseudo-folders auto-grouped by date, e.g. Today/Yesterday/Last week/June/2025) and "Folders" (the real user-created folder tree from the filesystem). Today these are rendered by **two entirely different component stacks**, not just different CSS:

- **Feed** — `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/feed-panel.tsx` always renders `<TreeNode>` (`ui/tree-node.tsx`) → `<TreeRow>` (`ui/tree-row.tsx`) for bucket rows and `<NavNoteRow>` (`ui/nav-note-row.tsx`) for note rows, with a `feedMode` boolean prop threaded through. Styling is hand-written CSS in `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css` (classes: `.item-row`, `.tree-pane .item-row`, `.feed-navigation-tree .item-row`, `.item-label`, `.note-count`, `.tree-guides`/`.tree-guide-vert`, `.icon-spacer`, `.tree-toggle`, `.folder-glyph`, `.feed-bucket-row`). Drag-and-drop hooks (`useDraggable`/`useDroppable` from `@dnd-kit/core`) exist in `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` but Feed explicitly passes `draggable={false}` (feed-panel.tsx ~line 235), and `edgeSnap={null}` always, since Feed has no manual reordering (grouping is purely by date).
- **Folders** — `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/folders-panel.tsx` has an `embedded` prop; it is **only ever called with `embedded={true}`** (single call site: `apps/desktop/src/desktop/desktop-app-shell.tsx` ~line 401). When `embedded`, `FoldersPanel` renders `<SidebarFileTreeNode>` (`ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx`) instead of `<TreeNode>` — a completely separate implementation built on shadcn/Tailwind `Sidebar*` primitives (`apps/desktop/src/shared/ui/sidebar.tsx`: `SidebarMenuButton`, `SidebarMenuSubButton`, `SidebarMenuSub`, `SidebarMenuBadge`, `SidebarMenuItem`). Its own doc comment literally says "without drag-and-drop" — `SidebarFileTreeNode` never calls `useDraggable`/`useDroppable`, so **folders currently cannot be drag-reordered or drag-moved in the UI at all**, even though the full DnD machinery (`apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/hooks/use-drag-drop.ts` — `useDragDrop` with `handleDragStart/handleDragMove/handleFolderDragEnd/handleNoteDragEnd`, wired into a `<DndContext>` in `desktop-app-shell.tsx` ~line 410) is fully implemented and only needs draggable row hooks to attach to. There is a *dead* non-embedded branch in `folders-panel.tsx` (`embedded={false}`) that also renders `<TreeNode>`, but it is never invoked in production — confirm/inspect this dead branch, since it may be reusable/removable rather than written from scratch.
- `folders-panel.tsx` was simplified in commit `4d727a9` ("Simplify notes navigation surfaces") which is what introduced `SidebarFileTreeNode` and dropped a `recent-tree-node.tsx` and DnD from the embedded path. This was an intentional past simplification by the repo owner, not an accidental bug — but the owner now wants folder/note drag-and-drop restored as part of this unification.

### The indentation bug (confirmed root cause)
When `shouldNestNotesInNavigation` is true (`notesListMode === "nested"` setting, computed in `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/state/use-notes-tree-state.ts` ~line 83), notes render inline inside their parent folder. In `SidebarFileTreeNode` (sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx), the folder row always renders either a toggle `<button className="sidebar-filetree-toggle">` (14x14) or `<span className="sidebar-filetree-toggle-spacer">` (14x14 placeholder) plus `gap: 8px` before the `<Folder />` glyph (~22px total reserved), but the sibling note row (`sidebar-filetree-note-button`) jumps straight to `<File />` with **no equivalent leading spacer** — so note labels sit ~22px left of sibling folder labels at the same nesting depth. By contrast, in the `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` stack (already used by Feed), `NavNoteRow` (`ui/nav-note-row.tsx`) always renders a matching `<span className="icon-spacer" />` (`.tree-pane .icon-spacer { width: 20px; height: 22px; }`, same as `.tree-pane .tree-toggle { width: 20px; height: 22px; }` in `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css`), so folder and note icons/labels align correctly there already.

### Hover/selected style difference (confirmed root cause)
`app.css` has base shared row rules under `.tree-pane .item-row` (hover `#f7f9fb`, selected `#f4f8ff` with `inset 2px 0 0 var(--ui-accent)` box-shadow, `border-radius: 0`, no horizontal padding on ancestors → edge-to-edge/full-bleed square-cornered highlight). # Unify Feed/Folders navigation onto one visual + component base

## Context

The desktop app's left nav has two tabs — **Feed** (pseudo-folders auto-grouped
by date) and **Folders** (the real filesystem folder tree) — that are meant to
feel like "the same tree" (shift-select, hover, selected state, expand/collapse)
but currently look and behave inconsistently. Investigation shows this isn't a
few stray CSS rules: the two tabs are rendered by **two entirely separate
component stacks**:

- **Feed** (`feed-panel.tsx`) always renders `TreeNode` → `TreeRow` /
  `NavNoteRow` (`ui/tree-node.tsx`, `ui/tree-row.tsx`, `ui/nav-note-row.tsx`) —
  hand-written CSS in `app.css`, dnd-kit hooks present but disabled
  (`draggable={false}`, since Feed buckets are date-derived and never
  reordered).
- **Folders** (`folders-panel.tsx`) is always called with `embedded` (its only
  call site, `desktop-app-shell.tsx:401`), which renders `SidebarFileTreeNode`
  (`ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx`) instead — a parallel implementation built on
  shadcn/Tailwind `Sidebar*` primitives, whose own doc comment says "without
  drag-and-drop." `folders-panel.tsx` also contains an **already-complete,
  currently-dead** non-embedded branch that renders through `TreeNode` exactly
  like Feed does (`renderTreeNodes()`, lines 90-114) — it was fully wired for
  drag/drop and simply stopped being invoked when the `embedded` sidebar
  redesign shipped (commit `4d727a9`, "Simplify notes navigation surfaces").

This split is the root cause of every symptom you flagged:
- **Hover/selected "full width" look** — Feed's rows are edge-to-edge,
  square-cornered (`app.css:616-633`, no ancestor padding); Folders' shadcn
  rows are a `rounded-md` pill inset by the sidebar's own padding, and Feed
  additionally overrides its hover/selected color under a `.feed-navigation-tree`
  scope (`app.css:805-820`) that Folders never gets.
- **Font "folders looks better"** — Folders' Tailwind `text-sm` rows default to
  regular weight and only go bold when the row is the active/selected one;
  Feed's `.item-label` is hard-coded to `font-weight: 500` (folders) / `450`
  (notes) *always*, regardless of selection.
- **Crooked nested-note indentation** — confirmed structural bug:
  `SidebarFileTreeNode`'s folder row always reserves a ~22px leading
  chevron/spacer + gap before the folder glyph; its note row
  (`sidebar-filetree-note-button`) has **no matching spacer** and jumps
  straight to the file icon, so note labels sit ~22px left of sibling folder
  labels at the same depth. `NavNoteRow` (already used by Feed) already renders
  a matching `.icon-spacer` and doesn't have this bug.
- **Bonus, discovered while investigating**: because `SidebarFileTreeNode`
  never calls `useDraggable`/`useDroppable`, **folder/note drag-and-drop is
  currently dead in the Folders tab**, even though the full reorder/move engine
  (`use-drag-drop.ts`, wired into a single shell-level `<DndContext>` in
  `desktop-app-shell.tsx:410-468`) is complete and only needs draggable rows to
  attach to. You confirmed you want this restored as part of the unification —
  you assumed folder/note drag-reorder already worked.
- Also as a side effect: `SidebarFileTreeNode` never sets `data-folder`/
  `data-note` attributes, so keyboard-driven "scroll selected row into view"
  (`use-keyboard-navigation.ts`) has been silently broken for the Folders tab;
  this gets fixed for free by the same migration.

**Your decisions** (from clarifying questions):
1. **Font**: adopt Folders' current behavior — regular weight by default, bold
   *only* on the selected row — for both tabs, but make note-row text a touch
   larger than Folders' current ~12.25px (aim ~13px, matching Feed's current
   note size).
2. **Guide lines** (vertical nesting connectors): show identically in both tabs
   (today Feed-only).
3. **Drag-and-drop**: Folders must get full manual drag/reorder/move for both
   folders and notes (this is expected core functionality). Feed keeps no
   reordering (grouped only by date) but keeps shift/cmd-click multi-select and
   context-menu delete/move — already working today, must not regress.

## Approach

Standardize both tabs on the `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` stack (the one
Feed already uses, and which `folders-panel.tsx` already has a working dead
branch for) and retire `SidebarFileTreeNode` entirely, rather than trying to
reconcile two parallel component trees. This turns every remaining difference
into a CSS/prop tweak instead of a duplicated implementation — exactly the
"one visual and component base" you asked for.

### 1. Component consolidation — `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/folders-panel.tsx`

- Remove the `embedded` prop and both branches gated on it (lines 43, 72,
  145, 148-178, 183-185). Keep exactly one render path: the existing
  `renderTreeNodes()` (lines 90-114) through `sectionContent`, unconditionally.
- Drop the `SidebarFileTreeNode` and `SidebarMenu` imports (lines 5, 7).
- `desktop-app-shell.tsx:401` — remove the `embedded` prop from the
  `<FoldersPanel>` call.
- Don't pass `draggable` or `feedMode` from `renderTreeNodes()` — leave them at
  their component defaults (`draggable = true` in `tree-node.tsx:64`,
  `feedMode = false`) so Folders becomes draggable and keeps folder (not
  calendar) glyphs automatically.
- Delete `ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx` outright (sole caller removed).
- Delete now-orphaned shadcn exports only used by it:
  `SidebarMenuBadge`/`SidebarMenuSub`/`SidebarMenuSubItem`/`SidebarMenuSubButton`
  in `shared/ui/sidebar.tsx`, and `shared/ui/collapsible.tsx` (Radix
  `Collapsible`/`CollapsibleContent` wrapper). Verify via grep before deleting
  that nothing else (in particular `app-sidebar.tsx`, which uses the *other*
  `Sidebar*` primitives for the outer app chrome) depends on them — leave
  everything else in `sidebar.tsx` untouched.

### 2. CSS reconciliation — `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css`

- Delete the Feed-only overrides at `805-829` (`.tree-pane .feed-navigation-tree
  .item-row` / `:hover` / `.selected` / `.tree-guides` / `.tree-guide-vert`).
  Once Folders renders through the same `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` DOM, the shared
  base rules at `616-633` (plain `#f7f9fb` hover / `#f4f8ff` selected with the
  inset accent bar, square corners, edge-to-edge — the look you preferred)
  become the single implementation for both tabs with no new CSS required.
  Keep `831-867` (`.feed-bucket-row` sizing/glyph rules) — those are
  legitimately Feed-specific and still gated by the `feedMode` prop, unrelated
  to this cleanup.
- During manual verification, confirm Folders rows still span full pane width
  without the deleted `width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box` (line 806-808) —
  port it into the base `.tree-pane .item-row` rule (616-624) if a regression
  shows up.
- Font hybrid: change `.tree-pane .item-label` (717-722) from always
  `font-weight: 500` to a regular default; drop the hard-coded
  `font-weight: 450` on `.tree-pane .nav-note-row .item-label` (643-646) so it
  falls through to the same default; add one new rule,
  `.tree-pane .item-row.selected .item-label { font-weight: 600; }`, placed
  after both of the above so it wins the cascade for both folder and note rows
  when selected. Keep note-row `font-size: 13px` (already matches the target).
- Mirror the same weight changes in the dark-theme block (`2592-2600`):
  drop the hard-coded weights on `.app.theme-dark .tree-pane .item-label` /
  `.nav-note-row .item-label` and add the dark-scoped
  `.app.theme-dark .tree-pane .item-row.selected .item-label { font-weight: 600; }`.
- Delete the now-dead `.sidebar-filetree-*` rules (`309-381`); keep
  `.sidebar-folders-section .nav-scroll-area`/`.pane-body` (296-307) only if
  `folders-panel.tsx` keeps using that class name on its wrapper — otherwise
  rename/remove to match.

### 3. Guide-line formula fix

- `ui/tree-row.tsx:82-84` — replace the `feedMode`-branching `guideBaseLeft`
  with the single unconditional formula `12 + indentationWidth / 2` (this is
  already what `nav-note-row.tsx:59` does unconditionally).
- `ui/tree-node.tsx:111` — remove `showGuides={feedMode}`; since guides are now
  always shown, drop the `showGuides` prop from `NavNoteRow` entirely
  (`nav-note-row.tsx` lines 17, 34, and the gate at line 75 becomes
  `{depth > 0 ? ... : null}`) — it has exactly one call site, so this is safe.

### 4. Indentation fix

No extra plumbing needed — this is fixed structurally by consolidating onto
`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`, whose `.icon-spacer`/`.tree-toggle` (both 20×22,
`app.css` ~749-803) already align folder and note rows at the same depth.
Verify pixel alignment manually after the migration (section 6) rather than
assuming it's resolved sight-unseen.

### 5. Drag-and-drop reconnection for Folders

No shell-level changes needed: `desktop-app-shell.tsx`'s single `<DndContext>`
(410-468) and its `useDragDrop()` call (236+) already operate on real folder
tree data (`tree`, `treeData`, `flatItems`, `orderedIds`, etc.) regardless of
which tab is active. The only missing link was `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`'s
`useDraggable`/`useDroppable` never mounting for Folders because
`SidebarFileTreeNode` didn't call them — step 1's migration reconnects
`handleDragStart/handleDragMove/handleFolderDragEnd/handleNoteDragEnd`
end-to-end for free, including the already-correct `edgeSnap` prop threading
(`desktop-app-shell.tsx:368` → `folders-panel.tsx:98` → `TreeNode`). No
backend/API changes needed (`moveItems`/`setOrder` calls in `use-drag-drop.ts`
are already shared, tested logic). Since Feed always passes `draggable={false}`,
Folders will be the first real exerciser of this drop-target code path in
production — budget extra manual testing time here rather than assuming parity
with Feed.

### Out of scope (flagged, not touched)

- `use-tree-interactions.ts` (folder click/rename handlers) and
  `feed-panel.tsx`'s inline click handlers stay as two separate
  implementations — they already both funnel into the same `TreeNode` props
  and share `computeRangeSelection`; the row-renderer swap doesn't require
  touching them.
- `use-keyboard-navigation.ts` vs `use-feed-keyboard-navigation.ts` stay
  separate; the `data-folder`/`data-note` scroll-into-view fix for Folders is a
  side effect of section 1, not a separate change.

## Critical files

- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/folders-panel.tsx` (consolidate to one render path)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx` (delete)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/tree-row.tsx` (guide formula)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/tree-node.tsx` (drop `showGuides={feedMode}`)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/nav-note-row.tsx` (drop `showGuides` prop)
- `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css` (hover/selected/font/guide consolidation, ~lines 296-381, 616-722, 805-867, 2579-2600)
- `apps/desktop/src/desktop/desktop-app-shell.tsx` (drop `embedded` prop at call site)
- `apps/desktop/src/shared/ui/sidebar.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/ui/collapsible.tsx` (trim dead exports, verify no other consumer first)

## Workflow

1. Create a git worktree for this work (as requested) via a new branch off
   `feat/react-native-monorepo`, e.g. `feature/unify-feed-folders-tree`.
2. Implement sections 1-3 together (they're interdependent — the CSS deletions
   only make sense once Folders actually renders through `TreeRow`).
3. Run `npm run desktop:dev` and manually verify (see below) before running
   automated checks.

## Verification

Run the desktop app (`npm run desktop:dev` or the Tauri shell if testing real
pointer-drag feel matters) and manually check:

1. Hover/selected on both tabs: edge-to-edge, square-cornered highlight,
   identical color in Feed and Folders.
2. Font: folder/note labels regular weight normally, bold only on the selected
   row, in both tabs; note text a bit larger/lighter than before, consistent
   between tabs.
3. Guide lines render identically at each depth in both tabs.
4. With `notesListMode` = nested, open a folder with both child folders and
   notes — labels line up at the same left edge; check the same in Feed.
5. Folder drag: drop-inside another folder, before/after a sibling (edge-snap
   reorder), and into the root drop zone — tree updates optimistically,
   `moveItems`/`setOrder` fire correctly.
6. Note drag: move a note to a different folder, reorder within a folder, drop
   onto another note.
7. Feed regression check: buckets/notes are still non-draggable; shift/cmd
   click range-select and right-click delete/move-to-folder still work.
8. Keyboard arrow navigation in Folders scrolls the selected row into view
   (previously broken).
9. Repeat 1-2 in dark theme.

Then run `npm run test` (Vitest — `tree-ops`, `feed-tree-model`,
`notes-tree-model` tests should be unaffected, this is UI/CSS/wiring only) and
`npm run typecheck` / `desktop:build` to confirm no build breakage from the
prop-shape trims (`FoldersPanelProps` losing `embedded`, `NavNoteRowProps`
losing `showGuides`) and the deleted files.

input.plan:
# Unify Feed/Folders navigation onto one visual + component base

## Context

The desktop app's left nav has two tabs — **Feed** (pseudo-folders auto-grouped
by date) and **Folders** (the real filesystem folder tree) — that are meant to
feel like "the same tree" (shift-select, hover, selected state, expand/collapse)
but currently look and behave inconsistently. Investigation shows this isn't a
few stray CSS rules: the two tabs are rendered by **two entirely separate
component stacks**:

- **Feed** (`feed-panel.tsx`) always renders `TreeNode` → `TreeRow` /
  `NavNoteRow` (`ui/tree-node.tsx`, `ui/tree-row.tsx`, `ui/nav-note-row.tsx`) —
  hand-written CSS in `app.css`, dnd-kit hooks present but disabled
  (`draggable={false}`, since Feed buckets are date-derived and never
  reordered).
- **Folders** (`folders-panel.tsx`) is always called with `embedded` (its only
  call site, `desktop-app-shell.tsx:401`), which renders `SidebarFileTreeNode`
  (`ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx`) instead — a parallel implementation built on
  shadcn/Tailwind `Sidebar*` primitives, whose own doc comment says "without
  drag-and-drop." `folders-panel.tsx` also contains an **already-complete,
  currently-dead** non-embedded branch that renders through `TreeNode` exactly
  like Feed does (`renderTreeNodes()`, lines 90-114) — it was fully wired for
  drag/drop and simply stopped being invoked when the `embedded` sidebar
  redesign shipped (commit `4d727a9`, "Simplify notes navigation surfaces").

This split is the root cause of every symptom you flagged:
- **Hover/selected "full width" look** — Feed's rows are edge-to-edge,
  square-cornered (`app.css:616-633`, no ancestor padding); Folders' shadcn
  rows are a `rounded-md` pill inset by the sidebar's own padding, and Feed
  additionally overrides its hover/selected color under a `.feed-navigation-tree`
  scope (`app.css:805-820`) that Folders never gets.
- **Font "folders looks better"** — Folders' Tailwind `text-sm` rows default to
  regular weight and only go bold when the row is the active/selected one;
  Feed's `.item-label` is hard-coded to `font-weight: 500` (folders) / `450`
  (notes) *always*, regardless of selection.
- **Crooked nested-note indentation** — confirmed structural bug:
  `SidebarFileTreeNode`'s folder row always reserves a ~22px leading
  chevron/spacer + gap before the folder glyph; its note row
  (`sidebar-filetree-note-button`) has **no matching spacer** and jumps
  straight to the file icon, so note labels sit ~22px left of sibling folder
  labels at the same depth. `NavNoteRow` (already used by Feed) already renders
  a matching `.icon-spacer` and doesn't have this bug.
- **Bonus, discovered while investigating**: because `SidebarFileTreeNode`
  never calls `useDraggable`/`useDroppable`, **folder/note drag-and-drop is
  currently dead in the Folders tab**, even though the full reorder/move engine
  (`use-drag-drop.ts`, wired into a single shell-level `<DndContext>` in
  `desktop-app-shell.tsx:410-468`) is complete and only needs draggable rows to
  attach to. You confirmed you want this restored as part of the unification —
  you assumed folder/note drag-reorder already worked.
- Also as a side effect: `SidebarFileTreeNode` never sets `data-folder`/
  `data-note` attributes, so keyboard-driven "scroll selected row into view"
  (`use-keyboard-navigation.ts`) has been silently broken for the Folders tab;
  this gets fixed for free by the same migration.

**Your decisions** (from clarifying questions):
1. **Font**: adopt Folders' current behavior — regular weight by default, bold
   *only* on the selected row — for both tabs, but make note-row text a touch
   larger than Folders' current ~12.25px (aim ~13px, matching Feed's current
   note size).
2. **Guide lines** (vertical nesting connectors): show identically in both tabs
   (today Feed-only).
3. **Drag-and-drop**: Folders must get full manual drag/reorder/move for both
   folders and notes (this is expected core functionality). Feed keeps no
   reordering (grouped only by date) but keeps shift/cmd-click multi-select and
   context-menu delete/move — already working today, must not regress.

## Approach

Standardize both tabs on the `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` stack (the one
Feed already uses, and which `folders-panel.tsx` already has a working dead
branch for) and retire `SidebarFileTreeNode` entirely, rather than trying to
reconcile two parallel component trees. This turns every remaining difference
into a CSS/prop tweak instead of a duplicated implementation — exactly the
"one visual and component base" you asked for.

### 1. Component consolidation — `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/folders-panel.tsx`

- Remove the `embedded` prop and both branches gated on it (lines 43, 72,
  145, 148-178, 183-185). Keep exactly one render path: the existing
  `renderTreeNodes()` (lines 90-114) through `sectionContent`, unconditionally.
- Drop the `SidebarFileTreeNode` and `SidebarMenu` imports (lines 5, 7).
- `desktop-app-shell.tsx:401` — remove the `embedded` prop from the
  `<FoldersPanel>` call.
- Don't pass `draggable` or `feedMode` from `renderTreeNodes()` — leave them at
  their component defaults (`draggable = true` in `tree-node.tsx:64`,
  `feedMode = false`) so Folders becomes draggable and keeps folder (not
  calendar) glyphs automatically.
- Delete `ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx` outright (sole caller removed).
- Delete now-orphaned shadcn exports only used by it:
  `SidebarMenuBadge`/`SidebarMenuSub`/`SidebarMenuSubItem`/`SidebarMenuSubButton`
  in `shared/ui/sidebar.tsx`, and `shared/ui/collapsible.tsx` (Radix
  `Collapsible`/`CollapsibleContent` wrapper). Verify via grep before deleting
  that nothing else (in particular `app-sidebar.tsx`, which uses the *other*
  `Sidebar*` primitives for the outer app chrome) depends on them — leave
  everything else in `sidebar.tsx` untouched.

### 2. CSS reconciliation — `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css`

- Delete the Feed-only overrides at `805-829` (`.tree-pane .feed-navigation-tree
  .item-row` / `:hover` / `.selected` / `.tree-guides` / `.tree-guide-vert`).
  Once Folders renders through the same `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` DOM, the shared
  base rules at `616-633` (plain `#f7f9fb` hover / `#f4f8ff` selected with the
  inset accent bar, square corners, edge-to-edge — the look you preferred)
  become the single implementation for both tabs with no new CSS required.
  Keep `831-867` (`.feed-bucket-row` sizing/glyph rules) — those are
  legitimately Feed-specific and still gated by the `feedMode` prop, unrelated
  to this cleanup.
- During manual verification, confirm Folders rows still span full pane width
  without the deleted `width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box` (line 806-808) —
  port it into the base `.tree-pane .item-row` rule (616-624) if a regression
  shows up.
- Font hybrid: change `.tree-pane .item-label` (717-722) from always
  `font-weight: 500` to a regular default; drop the hard-coded
  `font-weight: 450` on `.tree-pane .nav-note-row .item-label` (643-646) so it
  falls through to the same default; add one new rule,
  `.tree-pane .item-row.selected .item-label { font-weight: 600; }`, placed
  after both of the above so it wins the cascade for both folder and note rows
  when selected. Keep note-row `font-size: 13px` (already matches the target).
- Mirror the same weight changes in the dark-theme block (`2592-2600`):
  drop the hard-coded weights on `.app.theme-dark .tree-pane .item-label` /
  `.nav-note-row .item-label` and add the dark-scoped
  `.app.theme-dark .tree-pane .item-row.selected .item-label { font-weight: 600; }`.
- Delete the now-dead `.sidebar-filetree-*` rules (`309-381`); keep
  `.sidebar-folders-section .nav-scroll-area`/`.pane-body` (296-307) only if
  `folders-panel.tsx` keeps using that class name on its wrapper — otherwise
  rename/remove to match.

### 3. Guide-line formula fix

- `ui/tree-row.tsx:82-84` — replace the `feedMode`-branching `guideBaseLeft`
  with the single unconditional formula `12 + indentationWidth / 2` (this is
  already what `nav-note-row.tsx:59` does unconditionally).
- `ui/tree-node.tsx:111` — remove `showGuides={feedMode}`; since guides are now
  always shown, drop the `showGuides` prop from `NavNoteRow` entirely
  (`nav-note-row.tsx` lines 17, 34, and the gate at line 75 becomes
  `{depth > 0 ? ... : null}`) — it has exactly one call site, so this is safe.

### 4. Indentation fix

No extra plumbing needed — this is fixed structurally by consolidating onto
`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`, whose `.icon-spacer`/`.tree-toggle` (both 20×22,
`app.css` ~749-803) already align folder and note rows at the same depth.
Verify pixel alignment manually after the migration (section 6) rather than
assuming it's resolved sight-unseen.

### 5. Drag-and-drop reconnection for Folders

No shell-level changes needed: `desktop-app-shell.tsx`'s single `<DndContext>`
(410-468) and its `useDragDrop()` call (236+) already operate on real folder
tree data (`tree`, `treeData`, `flatItems`, `orderedIds`, etc.) regardless of
which tab is active. The only missing link was `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`'s
`useDraggable`/`useDroppable` never mounting for Folders because
`SidebarFileTreeNode` didn't call them — step 1's migration reconnects
`handleDragStart/handleDragMove/handleFolderDragEnd/handleNoteDragEnd`
end-to-end for free, including the already-correct `edgeSnap` prop threading
(`desktop-app-shell.tsx:368` → `folders-panel.tsx:98` → `TreeNode`). No
backend/API changes needed (`moveItems`/`setOrder` calls in `use-drag-drop.ts`
are already shared, tested logic). Since Feed always passes `draggable={false}`,
Folders will be the first real exerciser of this drop-target code path in
production — budget extra manual testing time here rather than assuming parity
with Feed.

### Out of scope (flagged, not touched)

- `use-tree-interactions.ts` (folder click/rename handlers) and
  `feed-panel.tsx`'s inline click handlers stay as two separate
  implementations — they already both funnel into the same `TreeNode` props
  and share `computeRangeSelection`; the row-renderer swap doesn't require

  already what `nav-note-row.tsx:59` does unconditionally).
- `ui/tree-node.tsx:111` — remove `showGuides={feedMode}`; since guides are now
  always shown, drop the `showGuides` prop from `NavNoteRow` entirely
  (`nav-note-row.tsx` lines 17, 34, and the gate at line 75 becomes
  `{depth > 0 ? ... : null}`) — it has exactly one call site, so this is safe.

### 4. Indentation fix

No extra plumbing needed — this is fixed structurally by consolidating onto
`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`, whose `.icon-spacer`/`.tree-toggle` (both 20×22,
`app.css` ~749-803) already align folder and note rows at the same depth.
Verify pixel alignment manually after the migration (section 6) rather than
assuming it's resolved sight-unseen.

### 5. Drag-and-drop reconnection for Folders

No shell-level changes needed: `desktop-app-shell.tsx`'s single `<DndContext>`
(410-468) and its `useDragDrop()` call (236+) already operate on real folder
tree data (`tree`, `treeData`, `flatItems`, `orderedIds`, etc.) regardless of
which tab is active. The only missing link was `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`'s
`useDraggable`/`useDroppable` never mounting for Folders because
`SidebarFileTreeNode` didn't call them — step 1's migration reconnects
`handleDragStart/handleDragMove/handleFolderDragEnd/handleNoteDragEnd`
end-to-end for free, including the already-correct `edgeSnap` prop threading
(`desktop-app-shell.tsx:368` → `folders-panel.tsx:98` → `TreeNode`). No
backend/API changes needed (`moveItems`/`setOrder` calls in `use-drag-drop.ts`
are already shared, tested logic). Since Feed always passes `draggable={false}`,
Folders will be the first real exerciser of this drop-target code path in
production — budget extra manual testing time here rather than assuming parity
with Feed.

### Out of scope (flagged, not touched)

- `use-tree-interactions.ts` (folder click/rename handlers) and
  `feed-panel.tsx`'s inline click handlers stay as two separate
  implementations — they already both funnel into the same `TreeNode` props
  and share `computeRangeSelection`; the row-renderer swap doesn't require
  touching them.
- `use-keyboard-navigation.ts` vs `use-feed-keyboard-navigation.ts` stay
  separate; the `data-folder`/`data-note` scroll-into-view fix for Folders is a
  side effect of section 1, not a separate change.

## Critical files

- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/folders-panel.tsx` (consolidate to one render path)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/sidebar-file-tree-node.tsx` (delete)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/tree-row.tsx` (guide formula)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/tree-node.tsx` (drop `showGuides={feedMode}`)
- `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/navigation/ui/nav-note-row.tsx` (drop `showGuides` prop)
- `apps/desktop/src/app/app.css` (hover/selected/font/guide consolidation, ~lines 296-381, 616-722, 805-867, 2579-2600)
- `apps/desktop/src/desktop/desktop-app-shell.tsx` (drop `embedded` prop at call site)
- `apps/desktop/src/shared/ui/sidebar.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/ui/collapsible.tsx` (trim dead exports, verify no other consumer first)

## Workflow

1. Create a git worktree for this work (as requested) via a new branch off
   `feat/react-native-monorepo`, e.g. `feature/unify-feed-folders-tree`.
2. Implement sections 1-3 together (they're interdependent — the CSS deletions
   only make sense once Folders actually renders through `TreeRow`).
3. Run `npm run desktop:dev` and manually verify (see below) before running
   automated checks.

## Verification

Run the desktop app (`npm run desktop:dev` or the Tauri shell if testing real
pointer-drag feel matters) and manually check:

1. Hover/selected on both tabs: edge-to-edge, square-cornered highlight,
   identical color in Feed and Folders.
2. Font: folder/note labels regular weight normally, bold only on the selected
   row, in both tabs; note text a bit larger/lighter than before, consistent
   between tabs.
3. Guide lines render identically at each depth in both tabs.
4. With `notesListMode` = nested, open a folder with both child folders and
   notes — labels line up at the same left edge; check the same in Feed.
5. Folder drag: drop-inside another folder, before/after a sibling (edge-snap
   reorder), and into the root drop zone — tree updates optimistically,
   `moveItems`/`setOrder` fire correctly.
6. Note drag: move a note to a different folder, reorder within a folder, drop
   onto another note.
7. Feed regression check: buckets/notes are still non-draggable; shift/cmd
   click range-select and right-click delete/move-to-folder still work.
8. Keyboard arrow navigation in Folders scrolls the selected row into view
   (previously broken).
9. Repeat 1-2 in dark theme.

Then run `npm run test` (Vitest — `tree-ops`, `feed-tree-model`,
`notes-tree-model` tests should be unaffected, this is UI/CSS/wiring only) and
`npm run typecheck` / `desktop:build` to confirm no build breakage from the
prop-shape trims (`FoldersPanelProps` losing `embedded`, `NavNoteRowProps`
losing `showGuides`) and the deleted files.

## Future work (explicitly deferred, not part of this task)

You want the tree row implementation to eventually be as much Tailwind and as
little hand-written CSS as possible. This plan consolidates on the opposite
stack (`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` + `app.css`) rather than the Tailwind/shadcn one
(`SidebarFileTreeNode`), because that stack already has working drag-and-drop
and the indentation bug fixed — doing it any other way would mean porting
dnd-kit hooks into a rewritten Tailwind component as part of this change,
which is riskier and out of scope for now. A separate future task should
rewrite `TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow` (and the `.item-row`/`.tree-guides`/
`.folder-glyph`/etc. rules in `app.css`) as Tailwind utility classes, carrying
over the dnd-kit wiring and the fixes made here, and retire the hand-written
CSS block for tree rows.

**Running means launching the actual app and interacting with it** —
not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its
window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md

- **Mega-repo, several plausible, no clear match** → ask the user
  which unit to run.
- **Stale** (fails on mechanics unrelated to your task) → tell the
  user; offer to refresh it via `/run-skill-generator`.
- **Nothing about running** → fall back to the patterns below.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's

# Example: Browser-driven web app

You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
headless container can't open a browser window — so "run the app" means
launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.

Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.

## Dev server

Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:

```bash
npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
echo $! > /tmp/dev.pid
timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
```

Don't `sleep 5` — poll the port. Stop with
`kill $(cat /tmp/dev.pid)` (or `pkill -f 'npm run dev'`) before
relaunching, or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`.

## Drive

`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:

```bash
chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
nav http://localhost:3000
wait-for text=Dashboard
screenshot
click button:has-text("New item")
fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
press Enter
wait-for text=Smoke test
screenshot
console --errors
EOF
```

Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` →
`wait-for` the element you need → act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
`press`) → `screenshot` → `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.

For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
at a time — same commands, same session.

**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver — the structure and commands
transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
drop the Electron-only window introspection
(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).

# Sprite Environment

## CRITICAL: Security Rules
- HTTP services you create may become PUBLIC - never expose secrets, env vars, or sensitive data
- See /.sprite/docs/agent-context.md for full security requirements

## Quick Reference

### URL
- Format: `https://<sprite-name>-<org>.sprites.dev/`
- Check yours: `sprite-env info` or `sprite url` (from outside)
- Auth modes: `sprite` (org members only, default) or `public` (open to internet)
- Proxy routes HTTP to the service with `--http-port`, or port 8080 by default

### Services
- Long-running processes that persist across reboots
- Create: `sprite-env services create <name> --cmd <command> [--http-port <port>]`
- Only one service can have `--http-port`; it auto-starts on incoming requests
- `--cmd` takes the binary only; pass arguments via `--args`: `--cmd python3 --args "-m,http.server,8080"`
- Do NOT start a background process separately — the service manages the process lifecycle
- Restart: `sprite-env services restart <name>` (do NOT use stop + start separately)
- List/start/stop/delete: `sprite-env services <subcommand>`
- Full help: `sprite-env services --help`

### Checkpoints
- Point-in-time snapshots of the writable filesystem overlay
- Create before risky changes, restore to roll back
- CLI: `sprite-env checkpoints create`, `sprite-env checkpoints list`

### Lifecycle
- Sprites run while servicing HTTP requests or while sessions generate output
- When idle, sprites pause automatically
- Services and sessions keep sprites alive
- Services restart automatically on boot

### Directory Layout
```
/.sprite/
  bin/              # sprite-env CLI — use this to manage services and checkpoints
  docs/             # Documentation (agent-context.md, languages.md)
  checkpoints/      # Last 5 checkpoints mounted here
  policy/           # Network egress policy (network.json)
  languages/        # Per-language llm.txt files
```

## Full Documentation

- /.sprite/docs/agent-context.md - Environment overview (URL, services, checkpoints, network policy)
- /.sprite/docs/languages.md     - Language runtimes and version managers

Per-language details: /.sprite/languages/<lang>/llm.txt

CLI help: `sprite-env --help`

content.text:
Реализация завершена. Итог:

**Что сделано** (в worktree `.claude/worktrees/unify-feed-folders-tree`, ветка `feature/unify-feed-folders-tree` от `feat/react-native-monorepo`):

1. **Folders** теперь рендерится через тот же стек `TreeNode`/`TreeRow`/`NavNoteRow`, что и Feed (удалён `SidebarFileTreeNode` и мёртвый `embedded`-код) — это разом чинит кривую индентацию вложенных заметок и возвращает drag-and-drop для папок и заметок (`useDragDrop` был полностью готов, просто не был подключён).
2. **Hover/selected**: убрана Feed-специфичная подсветка (`--sidebar-accent`), теперь оба таба используют единый edge-to-edge стиль с квадратными углами, который тебе понравился в Feed.
3. **Шрифт**: гибрид — обычный вес по умолчанию, bold только у выбранной строки (как в Folders), текст заметок ~13px (чуть крупнее, как просил).
4. **Guide lines**: показываются одинаково в обоих табах (раньше — только в Feed).
5. Весь CSS, относящийся к дереву навигации (включая переключатель вкладок Feed/Folders), вынесен в отдельный файл `features/notes/navigation/ui/tree.css`, подключаемый из `app.tsx`. В `app.css` остались только действительно общие для всего приложения примитивы (`.item-row`, `.item-label` и т.п. используются также note-row и settings-row).

**Проверено**: все тесты (54+10+6+18), `tsc --noEmit`, и полный `vite build` проходят чисто.

**Не проверено визуально**: приложение — Tauri-шелл, без бэкенда все IPC-вызовы падают (`invoke` undefined), поэтому в headless-браузере оно зависает на сплэше — это ожидаемо и не связано с моими правками (confirmed по консольным ошибкам). Полноценную визуальную/интерактивную проверку (hover, отступы, drag-and-drop) нужно сделать в реальном Tauri-приложении — вероятно, у тебя на Mac, судя по `MAC_BUILD_AND_TEST.md`.

Хочешь, чтобы я закоммитил изменения в этой ветке, или сначала сам всё посмотришь?

Полноценная визуальная и функциональная проверка выполнена (подменил Tauri backend через официальный `@tauri-apps/api/mocks`-подход, чтобы обойти отсутствие нативного шелла). Результаты:

**Визуально подтверждено** (скриншоты Folders/Feed, светлая и тёмная темы):
- **Hover/selected**: в обоих табах теперь одинаковый full-width, edge-to-edge, без скруглений стиль подсветки — ровно то, что просил.
- **Шрифт**: папки/заметки в обычном весе по умолчанию, **bold только у выбранной строки** — видно на примере активного "Today" в Feed (bold+подсветка) и невыбранных "Personal"/"Work Projects" в Folders (обычный вес).
- **Индентация**: заметки внутри папок (включая вложенные "Journal" → "entry one/two") теперь ровно выравниваются под именами родительских папок — старый баг с "кривой" индентацией пропал.
- Feed и Folders выглядят как один и тот же компонент — что и было целью.

**Функционально подтверждено**: перетащил заметку "budget" из "Work Projects" в "Personal" реальным pointer-drag (mousedown→move→up) — сработал `useDragDrop`, вызвался `invoke("move_items", { items: ["Work Projects/budget.md"], destination: "Personal" })` с корректными параметрами. Drag-and-drop в Folders действительно восстановлен и работает, а не только "должен работать по коду".

По пути поймал ложную тревогу (краш редактора при `read_note: null`) — оказалось это дыра в моём собственном IPC-моке, а не баг приложения.

Всё вместе: реализация полностью соответствует плану, автотесты/typecheck/build проходят, и теперь ещё и визуально-интерактивно проверено. Готов закоммитить изменения в ветке `feature/unify-feed-folders-tree` — коммитить?
